newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia woolgrowers to decide equity in j/v.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia woolgrowers to decide equity in j/v.

text.p: Australian woolgrowers will have a choice on whether they invest their Wool International (WI) equity in the proposed joint-venture company between Elders Australia Ltd, Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd and WI, WI chairman Dick Warburton said on Tuesday.

Woolgrowers would be invited through either a prospectus or an information memorandum to invest a portion of their equity in WI, which is responsible for selling Australia's two million bale wool stockpile, in the joint-venture, he said.
The proposed joint-venture company would be involved in wool merchanting, including forward trading and risk management, and wool handling to achieve logistical and marketiung efficiencies.

The services of the joint-venture company would be freely available to other wool brokers and access providers, Warburton said in a statement. He said he envisaged the company would be seeking from woolgrowers a level of equity which would represent only two to three percent of total woolgrower equity in WI.

Details of capital requirements for the joint-venture, in which all three parties will have an equal stake, are yet to be determined. Warburton said the latest estimates of WI's net worth or grower equity stood at about A$850 million in a range from A$700 million to A$1 billion.

For individual woolgrowers this represented an allocation of about A$2.40 for every A$1.00 of the 4.5 percent wool tax paid from July 1993 to June 1996. This equity is to be distributed to woolgrowers after the stockpile debt is repaid in 1998.
Mechanisms were now being considered by WI to facilitate woolgrowers investment in the joing venture, Warburton said.
Full details of the venture, including capital requirements, would be released later this month, Warburton said.
